title: Bollywood Demands Protection After Shroff Firing as Bishnoi Gang Issues Fresh Threat
excerpt: FWICE seeks a time-bound probe and enhanced security after the Juhu attack, as a purported Bishnoi post threatens anyone who works with Salman Khan and three suspects are detained in Kota.
body:
• The Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE) on Monday condemned the firing on Tiger Shroff in Juhu and demanded enhanced security for film personalities and a time-bound investigation.
  • A social media post attributed to Lawrence Bishnoi gang members Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu claimed responsibility and warned that anyone in Bollywood who works with Salman Khan "will be next" — a claim Mumbai Police have not confirmed.
  • Three men suspected of involvement were detained in Kota, Rajasthan, from a train coming from Mumbai, according to a police official cited by PTI.
  • Actors including Ravi Kishan and Ravie Dubey, who lives in the same building as Shroff, called the shooting a major security lapse and demanded the harshest punishment for those responsible.

A day after gunmen opened fire on Tiger Shroff's car in Mumbai's Juhu area, the fallout moved from the crime scene to the film industry itself. The Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE), the apex body of film workers, condemned the attack on Monday, demanded better protection for film personalities, and warned that this was the second firing involving a prominent industry figure, following the earlier incident involving filmmaker Rohit Shetty. Shroff, 36, escaped unhurt on Sunday evening; his driver and an autorickshaw driver were injured, according to police.

An Industry Body Demands a Time-Bound Probe

FWICE said such acts raise serious concerns about the safety of everyone associated with the industry and appealed to the Maharashtra government and police to act decisively. Its statement, reported by PTI via Filmibeat, sought an impartial investigation completed within a defined timeframe so those responsible are identified and brought to justice.

https://x.com/tv9gujarati/status/2112170461224440048

"Such acts of violence and intimidation are completely unacceptable and raise serious concerns about the safety and security of personalities associated with the Indian film industry."

— Federation of Western India Cine Employees (FWICE)

The body pointed to recurrence as the core problem. One firing can be treated as an aberration; a second attack on a leading film personality, after the Rohit Shetty incident, reads to the industry as a pattern that existing security arrangements are not deterring.

The Bishnoi Claim and the Salman Khan Threat

The security concern sharpened after a purported social media post by Lawrence Bishnoi gang member Anil Pandit claimed that he and Harman Sandhu were behind the attack. "We had called him and tried to make him understand, but he did not listen," the post read, according to The Business Standard, citing Hindustan Times. "Anyone in the Mumbai film industry who does not listen to us or works with Salman Khan will be next. Wait and watch."

Mumbai Police have not confirmed any link between the gang and the attack, and the authenticity of the post remains under verification — a distinction the industry coverage itself stresses. The claimed motive connects to the Bishnoi network's long-running hostility toward Salman Khan, which dates to the 1998 blackbuck poaching case; gunmen fired outside Khan's Bandra residence in April 2024. If police verify the claim, the Shroff attack would signal that the threat has widened from Khan himself to colleagues who work with him.

Colleagues Call It a Security Lapse

Reactions from within the industry mixed relief with anger. Actor and Member of Parliament Ravi Kishan described the shooting as deeply concerning, expressed confidence in the Maharashtra Police, and said those responsible should receive the harshest possible punishment, according to TellyChakkar. He described Shroff as an innocent and simple person and said he was grateful the actor escaped serious injury.

Actor Ravie Dubey, who lives in the same building as Shroff, went further, calling the incident a major security lapse. He expressed relief that Shroff was safe, noted that the actor's driver had been injured, and said swift arrests would bring relief to everyone concerned. Other actors, including Ahsaas Channa and Amol Parashar, voiced similar alarm in separate reactions, with Parashar saying news of gunfire sends panic through actors' families and that only consistent punishment deters further attacks.

What Happens Next

Police said three men suspected of involvement were detained in Kota from a Mumbai-bound train's route on Monday, while Mumbai Police's 15 teams continue examining CCTV footage and forensic evidence, as The Videshi reported in its earlier coverage of the attack. The immediate tests are whether police verify the Bishnoi claim, whether the detained men are charged, and whether the Maharashtra government answers FWICE's call with visible changes to protection for film personalities. Until then, an industry that, in the words echoed across Monday's reactions, thought the worst of the underworld era was behind it is confronting the possibility that it is not.
